- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.7), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 2–5% for next 5–10 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75% above recent mean), model frequently overcorrects; reduce forecast by 5–10% in next 3–7 days.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (price drops 5%+ from recent peak), model often fails to recognize it; reduce forecast by 3–8% for next 7–14 days.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently overestimates early in the horizon (first 5–7 days); apply downward bias of 1–3% for first 5 days.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead of true trend direction.
